title: Matter Tower
subject: Science: States of matter
intro: Solids, liquids, gases and the changes between them. A sample deck written for the plugin, not taken from any worksheet.

questions.q: Which state of matter keeps its own shape?
questions.explain: The particles of a solid are locked in place, so it keeps its shape. Liquids and gases take the shape of their container.

variants.q: An ice cube sits on a plate and stays a cube. Which state is it?

steps.q: Does water in a glass keep its own shape?
choices: No, it takes the shape of the glass

steps.q: Does a rock change shape when you move it to a bowl?

questions.q: Which state spreads out to fill its whole container?
questions.explain: Gas particles move freely and far apart, so a gas fills any container it is in.

variants.q: Air let out of a balloon spreads through the room. Which state is air?

questions.q: A ______ has a fixed volume but takes the shape of its container.
questions.explain: A liquid keeps the same amount of space (volume) but flows to fit its container.

variants.q: Juice poured from a carton into a cup changes shape but not amount. Juice is a ______.

questions.q: What is it called when a solid turns into a liquid?
questions.explain: Melting is solid to liquid. It happens when the solid gains enough heat.

variants.q: Butter in a hot pan turns runny. Which change is that?

questions.q: What is it called when a liquid turns into a solid?
questions.explain: Freezing is liquid to solid. It happens when the liquid loses heat.

variants.q: A puddle turns to ice overnight. Which change is that?

questions.q: A puddle dries up on a sunny day because the liquid water turned into gas. This change is called ______.
questions.explain: Evaporation is liquid to gas. Heat from the sun gives water particles enough energy to leave as water vapor.

variants.q: Wet clothes dry on a line because the water goes into the air. This is ______.

questions.q: Water drops form on the outside of a cold glass. Which change made them?
questions.explain: Condensation is gas to liquid: water vapor in the air cools on the glass and becomes liquid drops.
questions.review: Drops on a cold glass = condensation

variants.q: A bathroom mirror fogs up after a hot shower. Which change is that?

steps.q: Where did the water on the glass come from?
choices: From water vapor in the air

questions.q: What happens to particles when matter is heated?
questions.explain: Heat is energy. Particles that gain energy move faster and spread apart.

variants.q: A pot of water is put on a hot stove. Its particles...

questions.q: In which state are particles packed most tightly?
questions.explain: Solid particles are packed tightly and only vibrate in place. That is why solids keep their shape.
Water freezes (and ice melts) at 0 degrees Celsius.

variants.q: Ice begins to melt when it warms to ______ degrees Celsius.

questions.q: At sea level, water boils at what temperature?
questions.explain: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level (that is 212 degrees Fahrenheit, not Celsius).

questions.q: A chocolate bar left in a hot car turns soft and runny. What happened?
choices: The chocolate gained heat and melted
The chocolate lost heat and froze
The chocolate gained heat and condensed
The car lost heat and evaporated
questions.explain: The chocolate took in heat from the hot car. A solid gaining heat and becoming liquid is melting.
